title: Bob Red Cross's room and rehearsing at the Chicago union hall
summary: Musicians walk daily from the Michigan Hotel to the union hall, where Tubby Hall cooks red beans and rice, and Budd mentions a photo of Ben Webster.

story.theme_name: Chicago: the jazz migration and its clubs
story.community_name: Going north: working the Chicago jazz scene

blocks.x: I believe his last name was Washington too. But any way we used to walk -- Bob Red Cross had a little pad at the Michigan Hotel.
Bob Red Cross was the connection man.

He was the connection. And Bird and everybody used to hang out in his room. He had a room right on the first floor of the hotel. We used to sit in there and get (inaudible) and make little home recordings and things. We used to walk from there all the way down -- where was the union, 23rd and State?
39th and State. Walk all the way down there to rehearse every day.
I tell you, Tommy and Milt just gave me a beautiful picture of Ben Webster, and this was taken in Beef Steak Charlie's which is now closed, but it's called another name. Was it?

I wish you could see this picture of Ben, it's beautiful. And any way we used to walk down there and rehearse every day. Well now Tubby Hall was the drummer that used to play with Louis years ago. He was up to the union and he's from New Orleans, so he would put on those pots for us, red beans and rice and things like that, and we'd chip in and give him the money and he would cook these pots. And we would eat up to the union and rehearse. We didn't have to pay no money for the rehearsal hall, we didn't have to pay anything. So we were able to rehearse there.
